text:
alex: Heads-up: I'm preparing a small docs update to clarify Dedicated autoscale "burst" behavior and add a YAML example for burst_capacity. Need reviewers for wording and SDK snippets. I'll attach a draft PR after lunch.

meera: I can review wording and the SLA blurb. We should clarify "burst credits" vs "burst_capacity" to avoid customer confusion. Suggest wording: 'Burst capacity is short-lived excess throughput allocated per pool; it's not included in committed capacity and is subject to preemption under strict isolation.'

ryan.j: I'll take the Python SDK snippet and a short note for the API changelog. Any preferred default for burst_capacity in examples?

frank: Can do the Terraform + console copy. For examples let's pick realistic numbers: burst_capacity: 200, baseline_replicas: 4, max_scale_replicas: 12. Also need to reconcile the SLA table row for "burst" — currently the SLA only references reserved capacity which confuses support tickets.

docs-bot: link-checker: dedicated/autoscale.md -> broken internal link at line 78: `#burst-behaviour` (typo). Suggested anchor: `#burst-behavior`.

alex: Good catch. Also the migration lint requires frontmatter `migration: yes` if we include instructions for customers on config rename (we're renaming `burst_limit` -> `burst_capacity`).

meera: draft language for the SLA note: 'Burst capacity is opportunistic and best-effort. Customers relying on strict SLAs should provision dedicated baseline capacity or use strict isolation with pinned fallback models.' Feedback?

ryan.j: Python snippet I'll add (with syntax tag):
```python
# create scale policy with burst capacity
policy = {
  "name": "bursty-workloads",
  "baseline_replicas": 4,
  "max_scale_replicas": 12,
  "burst_capacity": 200,
  "isolation_level": "balanced",
}
client.dedicated.create_scale_policy(policy)
```
I'll also add a migration note: `burst_limit` -> `burst_capacity` + example of how to calculate approximate cost impact.

frank: Terraform example (will add language tag):
```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_scale_policy" "burst" {
  name               = "bursty-workloads"
  baseline_replicas  = 4
  max_scale_replicas = 12
  burst_capacity     = 200
  isolation_level    = "balanced"
}
```
I'll patch the console copy to mention "burst credits" as temporary and show a tooltip in UI.

docs-bot: preview build: autoscale.md -> warnings: missing code block language tag on one snippet; broken anchor flagged.

linter-bot: style-check: please avoid passive voice in provisioning intro; prefer short imperative sentences. Also add `migration: yes` to frontmatter if including migration section.

alex: Plan: I'll open PR today and mark it as draft. tagging @meera and @frank for review. After merge, we'll ask support to update FAQ and add a short KB article about how burst impacts billing and SLAs.

meera: Sounds good. One more content ask: add a one-line example for regulated workloads recommending `isolation_level: strict` and call out that burst_capacity may be disabled in that mode. I'll drop that as an inline suggestion in the PR.

ryan.j: PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/456 — contains wording, Python + Terraform snippets, and SLA note.

frank: I'll push a small follow-up PR to fix the anchor and console crosslink if IO isn't blocked by the merge order.

alex: Thanks everyone. Aim to merge before the PM sync tomorrow so the release notes can reference it. :rocket:
